title: The Evolution of Urban Green Spaces

sections.heading: Reading Passage 1
sections.passage: Urban green spaces have undergone significant transformation over the last few decades. Once merely seen as patches of grass and trees, these areas have evolved into essential components of urban environments. Research indicates that green spaces contribute not only to the aesthetic appeal of cities but also to public health and ecological benefits. Parks, gardens, and green roofs play crucial roles in urban ecology, serving as habitats for various species and helping mitigate urban heat. Furthermore, studies have shown that access to green spaces positively influences mental health, reducing stress and anxiety levels among city dwellers. The concept of 'biophilia,' which suggests that humans have an innate affinity for nature, supports the integration of greenery into urban planning. However, challenges remain in equitable access to these spaces, particularly in low-income neighborhoods where green areas are often scarce. Recent initiatives aim to address these disparities by advocating for the transformation of neglected spaces into community gardens and parks. By fostering biodiversity and enhancing residents' quality of life, urban green spaces are vital to the sustainability of modern cities.
